angle: The issue where the pilot appealed the bench's own clean bill — 'zero swaps left' failed a de-biased re-verification, three cards moved, the tenth Game Changer arrived — while the verified fifteen-cast table-kill at the center didn't move an inch: v4 bought instant-speed access to it, a sweep-proof clock, and interaction that is never dead.

Everyone pays.' stays directly under the deck name. Every promise above is checker-passed (stacks 001, 004, 005, 006), a committed artifact figure, or the documented re-verification story in sideboard_analysis.json and HISTORY.md. Do not add a third violator, and do not tease the unverified candidates: the Archive-halved ledger, the Drannith stranding lock, the Monastery Mentor loop payoff, and the Jace self-deck win are 'needs a stack scenario' everywhere they appear.

Two-bucket contents plus the tier legend printed in full — Vol. 004 updated thrice, but every issue is somebody's first. In THIS ISSUE'S DECK, the one-line promise for The Kill should read 'one verified table-kill, two famous fakes' so the arc is promised from page two. The contents blurb for Upgrade Watch may promise the process story plainly: 'the verdict we printed last time didn't survive our own re-check — good.' By the Numbers' blurb notes the fresh 10,000-game simulation on the new sha (284067d77208).

departments.headline: THE GENEROSITY TRAP
departments.dek: Why would a control deck hand every opponent an extra card, every turn, on purpose — and then add a rabbit who gives them life too? Because in this court the cards aren't a gift, they're evidence, the sentence is read at each opponent's upkeep — and as of this printing, the execution can be scheduled a turn in advance.

callouts.title: LOOK LIKE A GIFT
callouts.text: Turns one through three are Remora into rock into Kami — or Kwain, whose tap hands everyone a card and a life and makes the whole table like you. Eighteen lands plus a load-bearing rock suite keep you on schedule while the pod files you under harmless, and every card an opponent accepts inches them toward the punisher thresholds.

callouts.title: LAND THE HINGE
callouts.text: Heliod arrives on turn 4 in the majority of simulated games — 5,115 of 10,000 on turn 4 exactly, 89.6% by turn 6. The front face rebuys an enchantment on arrival; the {3}{U/P} flip into the Warped Eclipse is the moment the deck turns on, and it can only ever happen at sorcery speed.

callouts.title: OPEN THE COURT
callouts.text: The Warped Eclipse grants everything flash and discounts your spells {1} for each card your opponents drew this turn. Your own Mines pay your mana bill — and the hug layer feeds it on demand: a Kwain activation or a Second Doctor end-step offer grows the discount on exactly the turn you want to act.

callouts.title: PASS SENTENCE — OR EXECUTE
callouts.text: The punishers convert hand size into upkeep damage: once Forced Fruition fills a hand, cleanup trims it to exactly seven and the next upkeep costs them 7, verified and repeating without you tapping a land. And the deck still holds what no earlier printing of this issue could promise: a checker-stamped one-turn table-kill. The moment Hullbreaker Horror, both rocks, and Aetherflux Reservoir line up behind a Grand Abolisher, you stop playing fair — and Enlightened Tutor, new this printing, can put the missing piece on top of your library the end step before.

captions.Howling Mine: **THE BAIT:** an extra card for everyone at each draw step. Perfectly symmetric on its face — the punishers and Heliod's discount are what make it yours.
captions.Kwain, Itinerant Meddler: **THE HANDSHAKE:** everyone draws, drawers gain a life, and the table likes you — while every accepted card feeds the punisher math and Heliod's discount. Two mana buys the waiting turns this deck lives on.
captions.Forced Fruition: **THE DETONATOR:** every opponent spell becomes seven forced draws. Nobody stays under the punisher threshold once this resolves.

pilot_tips.text: Check your opener for Leyline of Anticipation — it comes down free before turn one and makes every engine piece a flash play, which is Heliod's back face a full three turns early.

departments.pull_quote: The cards aren't a gift. They're evidence.

departments.headline: THEIR DRAWS, YOUR DISCOUNT
departments.dek: Your commander is the one card you are guaranteed to have — so what is that worth when the card is a hinge the whole deck turns on? Here, it is the single most reliable event in 10,000 simulations, and the tax math has a wrinkle no other deck in this series has had.
departments.body: Start with the guarantee. The command zone means Heliod is not a card you hope to draw: he is face up before the first mulligan is offered, and the simulator confirms what guaranteed access is worth — mean cast turn 4.161, median 4, down by turn 6 in 89.6% of games, the most dependable number in the whole issue. That is why Keep or Ship never asks your opening hand for a commander, an engine payoff, or a win condition: the deck's hinge is already on the table, and your seven cards only need to buy the turns before him. The tax ladder reads 4, then 6, then 8, then 10 — but this commander's real recast cost is the wrinkle: Heliod always returns front-face-up, so every recast is tax PLUS another {3}{U/P} PLUS another sorcery-speed window you may never safely get. That math is why protection beats recasting here more decisively than usual — and in this list the insurance is countermagic, not equipment: free or cheap interaction is in hand by turn 6 in 67.2% of games, and the Phyrexian pip is itself a sequencing lever, because paying the flip with 2 life instead of {U} keeps a whole Counterspell live through the one activation this deck can never take reactively. Color identity is its own lesson: the front face is mono-white, but a double-faced card's identity is the union of its faces, and the blue back face is the entire reason this is a WU deck — the operating color too: 61 blue pips across 40 cards against 16 white pips across 14, with six blue-producing lands against a source target of 36, which is why the rocks and duals carry the deck. V4 even priced the pip load out loud: Archmage's Charm is the deck's only triple-pip card, and Karsten's tables want 37 blue sources to promise {U}{U}{U} on curve — this deck targets 36, so the Charm is a turn-4-plus spell cast off duals and Heliod's discount, never a turn-3 promise. The 21-damage clock, for once, is a coincidence: a 4/4 needs six connections and this deck plans zero of them. And the political read: the Radiant Dawn resolving next to a Kwain looks like the friendliest board in the format, and the table will treat it that way — but a turn-one Rhystic Study tells every experienced pilot what bracket you actually are, because this list's floor is 4 on the strength of ten Game Changers alone. The zone guarantees the hinge; the format guarantees the tell.

captions.Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the: **THE HINGE:** the front face rebuys an enchantment on arrival; the {3}{U/P} flip — sorcery speed only, 2 life if you're short a blue — makes your whole deck flash and bills your spells to the table's draw count.
captions.Fierce Guardianship: **THE INSURANCE:** a free 'no' while your commander is on the battlefield. An answered Heliod costs tax, another {3}{U/P}, and a sorcery window you may never get back — this counter is cheaper than all three.

pilot_tips.card: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse
pilot_tips.text: Pay the flip's {U/P} with 2 life on the turn you transform — two life out of a healthy total converts directly into one fully live counterspell across the only window where Heliod is exposed.

departments.pull_quote: You are not protecting a 4/4. You are protecting a sorcery-speed activation you only get to take while he lives.

departments.headline: THE SWAPS, MEASURED
departments.dek: Three cards in, three cards out — so what did the trade actually buy? We ran the v4 list another 10,000 times on seed 42, and the ledger answers with a number magazines never print on purpose: flat. The wincon meter didn't move — and that flat line is the whole story.

callouts.title: 73.4% KEEPABLE
callouts.text: 73.4% of first sevens are keeps at 0.336 mulligans per game. Eighteen lands sounds reckless until you see the kept-hand distribution centered on 2–3 lands plus rocks — the mana rocks are load-bearing, not filler.

callouts.title: TURN 4, LIKE CLOCKWORK
callouts.text: The commander histogram spikes at turn 4 — 5,115 of 10,000 games — with mean 4.161 and 89.6% by turn 6. Heliod is the most reliable event in the deck; the plan can afford patience everywhere else because the hinge shows up on a date.

callouts.title: THE FREE TRADE: 49.6%
callouts.text: Win-condition access by turn 6 reads 49.6% — 61.2% ever, mean turn 3.207 — against 50.1% before the swaps, with Enlightened Tutor now standing in Secure the Wastes' place in the access group. Half a point is noise, and we refuse to round it into a win: the honest finding is that the deck traded token wincon breadth for kill-line depth at no measured access cost.

callouts.title: THE ENGINE HELD: 41.3%
callouts.text: 'Engine + punisher assembled', the deck's core two-piece, lands by turn 6 in 41.3% of games — 56.6% ever, mean turn 4.176 — and still a minority: in most games you open as a draw-go control deck waiting for the court to convene. The deck is built to be good at exactly that.

callouts.title: SAYING NO IN 77.8%
callouts.text: Free or cheap interaction is in hand by turn 6 in 67.2% of games and 77.8% overall — up five points from the last printing, which is Archmage's Charm joining the suite and doing exactly what it was drafted to do. Holding up an answer is not a fallback plan; it is the statistically dominant line.

captions.Thought Vessel: **LAB NOTE:** rocks contribute from the turn after they land in this model — and mean available mana still hits 4.113 on turn 4 and 4.751 on turn 5. Heliod on four, the flip on five: the schedule pays for itself.

pilot_tips.text: Lead Ancient Tomb into a two-mana rock whenever the opener offers it — that line is how 27.3% of simulated games put Heliod down by turn 3.

departments.pull_quote: Access held at 49.6 against 50.1 — flat, and we print it flat. The deck swapped breadth for depth, and the meter says the trade was free.
departments.note: The stated-assumptions box is non-negotiable and earns its keep three times here: the model simulates resource development, not games; it does not model cost reducers, so every number on this page ignores Heliod's discount entirely — the real deck is faster than the chart, the chart is the floor; and it does not play tutors, so Enlightened Tutor counts in the access group as a drawn card only — its instant-speed fetch is upside the meter cannot see. Say all three exactly that plainly, in the lab voice. Cite the sha (284067d77208) so nobody mistakes these for any previous build's figures.

departments.headline: THE EXECUTION LEDGER
departments.dek: The database's two-card infinite died in file one. What the checker built from the wreckage is better than the myth: fifteen casts, three fifty-point payments, three dead opponents, one main phase — and a two-mana creature that locks the courtroom doors while a one-mana tutor schedules the date.

callouts.title: THE ENGINE, ESTABLISHED
callouts.text: Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + Arcane Signet: each rock's cast bounces the other, and tapping each for its mana while the bounce trigger waits keeps the cycle at exactly 3 mana in, 3 out. Mana-neutral, so the cast count is unbounded within one main phase off a {2} investment. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-004.

callouts.title: THE CONVERTER
callouts.text: Aetherflux Reservoir turns the count into life: 'gain 1 life for each spell you've cast this turn' means cast n nets +n, so k casts pay out k(k+1)/2 — triangular growth on a loop that costs nothing to run.

callouts.title: FIFTEEN, PROVEN
callouts.text: From 32 life the gains must reach 119. Fifteen casts pay 120 and clear the bar; fourteen pay only 105 and fail. That is the checker-stamped minimum — not a vibe, an inequality. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-006.

callouts.title: THREE PAYMENTS, THREE BODIES
callouts.text: The verified schedule: casts 1–6 lift you to 53, and the first 'Pay 50 life: deal 50 damage' drops you to 3 and kills the 26-life seat via state-based actions. Casts 7–12 rebuild to 60; the second payment (60 to 10) takes the 40-life seat. Casts 13–15 reach 52; the third (52 to 2) takes the last — and with every opponent gone, you win on the spot, alive at 2.

callouts.title: THE VERIFIED WEAKNESS
callouts.text: The same case file names the flaw: every loop cast and every activation opens a fully open priority window. Activating an ability is not casting a spell, so Hullbreaker never triggers on it, and the sorcery-speed loop pieces can only be cast with the stack empty — the engine cannot respond to anything, ever.

callouts.title: THE DOORMAN
callouts.text: Grand Abolisher is in the 99 for exactly that hole: during your turn, opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments — the named answer to the windows the kill opens. Cast it first on the commit turn: its cast is #1 on the Reservoir's own ledger, and the only interactable moment left is the response to Abolisher itself, while the expensive pieces are still safe in hand.

callouts.title: PLANS B AND C, ALSO STAMPED
callouts.text: Approach of the Second Sun's second cast wins during resolution — the only window is while it sits on the stack, and the case file plays out the counter-war, Swan Song included (A-002). And the punisher clock still runs the long game: Forced Fruition fills a hand, cleanup trims it to seven, and the next upkeep costs 7 without you tapping a land (A-003).

callouts.title: TWO FAMOUS FAKES
callouts.text: The refutation pair remains the credibility page: A-001 kills the two-card 'infinite' 296,000 database decks believe in — the Horror's trigger locks its target while Sol Ring is still a spell — and A-005 kills our own hope that Displacer Kitten makes the loop mana-positive: blink and bounce are mutually exclusive on every cast, and the Kitten's best trick is a one-time exit worth 3 floating mana.

captions.Hullbreaker Horror: **THE SPINE:** an uncounterable flash 7/8 whose cast trigger runs the whole engine — and gives the kill zero protection, because activating the Reservoir is not casting.
captions.Aetherflux Reservoir: **THE CONVERTER:** cast n nets +n life, and 'Pay 50 life: deal 50 damage' is paid before anyone can respond. Fifteen casts from 32 life is the proven minimum.
captions.Arcane Signet: **CAST #1:** in the verified walk the humble Signet opens the ledger — its cast bounces Sol Ring, its tap keeps the cycle at exactly 3-in, 3-out.
captions.Grand Abolisher: **THE DOORMAN:** two mana closes every priority window the kill opens — for your whole turn.
captions.Enlightened Tutor: **THE SCHEDULER:** new this printing — one white mana at instant speed puts any artifact piece of the kill on top of your library. Everything but Hullbreaker himself is now an end-step decision away.
captions.Approach of the Second Sun: **THE CLEAN EXIT:** the win is checked mid-resolution, not by state-based action, and the first casting counts even though the card was shuffled away. Once every player passes on the second cast, nothing stops it.
captions.Displacer Kitten: **THE HOPE, AUDITED:** every noncreature cast blinks something — but never the thing the Horror is already bouncing. The loop stays 3-in, 3-out, and unbounded mana does not exist.

pilot_tips.text: Lead the commit turn with Grand Abolisher, not the turn before — telegraphed a rotation early he is removal bait and an announcement; cast first on the go turn he closes the windows, counts toward the ledger, and leaves only his own response window open.

Recount the minimum from your actual life before you go: the gains must reach 151 minus your life total, so 15 casts at 32 life becomes 16 at 20 and 17 at 8 — every point of chip damage you absorbed is another cast on the bill.

Fire Enlightened Tutor on the end step before your commit turn — it tops the Reservoir or the missing rock, your draw step delivers it, and the table never sees a three-of-four board sitting in the open.
Hold Swan Song for the counter-war on the second Approach — a 2/2 Bird is a bargain against winning the game, and the case file shows exactly where it slots into the stack.

departments.pull_quote: Fourteen casts pay 105 and fail. Fifteen pay 120. The difference between a threat and a kill is an inequality, and the checker signed it.
departments.note: A-006 is the marquee spread and gets the most ambitious layout of the volume: the full execution ledger as the scene, the three payments as the numbered sequence, the open-window caveat printed beside the payoff — the verified weakness is part of the verified fact, never a footnote. A-004 runs second as the engine room, A-002 third, A-003 fourth, then the refutation pair A-001 + A-005 as the linked double spread. The v4 swaps touched none of the six case files — every cited card is still in the 99, and the loop's rock pair is Sol Ring + Arcane Signet with Thought Vessel the verified exact substitute. Citations stay in Judge's Desk; this department narrates. Three tier-discipline flags: the Abolisher-closes-the-windows claim rides stack 006's own steps and oracle text, but whether the shield is airtight — the channel-lands loophole, Otawara activating from hand — has no walkthrough yet, so any 'uninterruptable' phrasing must be coach-voiced, not stamped. The Enlightened Tutor scheduling line is oracle text plus coaching, never stamped. And the Alhammarret's Archive doubled-ledger extension is a flagged candidate, not a fact: the printed minimum is 15.

departments.headline: EVERYONE KNOWS THE MATH
departments.dek: At a bracket-4 table your Rhystic Study is priced in and your Sol Ring is furniture — so which cards on your board actually announce the kill, and why is the right answer to keep one in your hand and fire the other at an end step you chose?

callouts.title: THREAT WINDOW
callouts.text: Aetherflux Reservoir next to Hullbreaker Horror is the loudest board state you can present: anyone who has done the reading runs stack 006's arithmetic on sight — mana-neutral loop, triangular life, three 50-point payments, dead table — and every removal spell and counter in the pod turns toward you that instant. Hullbreaker alone reads as a flash fatty; the rocks read as furniture. The Reservoir is the tell, so it is the LAST piece you deploy — on the commit turn itself, never a turn early to 'develop.'

callouts.title: THE ONE DELIBERATE TELEGRAPH
callouts.text: There is exactly one board where an early Reservoir is right: the punisher clock already public — stack 003's upkeep arithmetic on the table — and free counters in hand. Then the visible Reservoir soaks the artifact removal that would otherwise dismantle Iron Maiden or the Mine layer, and the archenemy mantle freezes a pod whose upkeeps are bleeding. That is embracing the threat on your terms. Every other early Reservoir is donating information.

callouts.title: ABOLISHER GOES FIRST
callouts.text: The commit turn is still this deck's central play skill, and the sequencing rule is strict: Grand Abolisher is cast ON the go turn, as its first spell — not the turn before, whatever your instincts say about setup. A telegraphed Abolisher sitting through a full rotation is removal bait and an announcement; cast first on the go turn he closes every window for the rest of the turn, counts as cast #1 toward the ledger, and exposes only his own response window while the expensive pieces are still in hand.

callouts.title: SCAN BEFORE YOU GO
callouts.text: Two classes of card beat Abolisher because they are not responses: a Rule of Law-class static already on the battlefield ends a 15-cast line outright, and a Thalia- or Trinisphere-class tax breaks the loop's verified mana-neutrality. Scan the table for those BEFORE the commit. And respect the ugliest out: the verified ledger has you at 3 life after the first payment, so a damage-redirect effect in an open window kills YOU with your own Reservoir.

callouts.title: THE TUTOR IS A TELL, TOO
callouts.text: Enlightened Tutor is this printing's new information problem, cutting both ways. Fired early it reads as value — a punisher, a tax piece, a doubler. Fired at an end step, late, from a deck whose Reservoir kill is public knowledge, it says 'the go turn is my untap' to anyone paying attention. So spend it on the information schedule you choose: the late, end-step version happens behind untapped counter mana, or on a turn when nothing on your board looks like three-of-four.

callouts.title: THE MAGISTRATE'S MASS
callouts.text: Drannith Magistrate carries its own political weight. Cast turn 2 into a fresh pod, it unites three commander-dependent players against you for no return; cast when one commander is the table's shared problem, it is coalition glue two opponents will actively protect. Treat it as both magnet and bargaining chip — and don't promise anyone the stranding lock with Verdict or Path, because no stack has walked it.

captions.Aetherflux Reservoir: **THE SANDBAG:** the one card on your board that does stack 006's math out loud. It stays in hand until the turn it wins.
captions.Rhystic Study: **PRICED IN:** turn-2 Study draws groans, not removal, at this tier — but it tells every experienced pilot what the hug costume is hiding: a ten-Game-Changer, floor-4 list.
captions.Jace Beleren: **THE GIFT THAT TICKS:** the +2 hands every player a card and reads as generosity — while feeding Heliod's discount and the punisher thresholds from three opponents at once, behind loyalty no creature wrath touches.

pilot_tips.text: In the control mirror, say 'it can't be countered' out loud before you need it — the uncounterable wrath is a political instrument that redirects the board-committing player's aggression somewhere else.
Spend Teferi's Protection on the Farewell-class sweeper, not the alpha strike — it phases out your entire punisher board, which is the asset the attack was never going to touch.

departments.pull_quote: Every other early Reservoir is donating information.

departments.headline: TWO TABLES, NO TAKEBACKS
departments.dek: One turn asks whether generosity is safe with a spellslinger across the table; the other asks when a god should change faces. Read each board, commit out loud, and only then read the bench's ruling.

callouts.title: HOW TO PLAY ALONG
callouts.text: Cover the recommendation box with your hand. Read the board, pick a branch, say it out loud — the signals and coalition risks are printed with each branch precisely so you can argue with them. Being wrong on this page is free; being wrong at the table costs a game.

pilot_tips.text: Deploy Dictate of Kruphix at the end of the turn before the upkeep you most want taxed — flash means the extra draws start exactly where you point them.
Use Folio of Fancies' X-activation as a precision tool: push exactly the hand you want over seven, exactly when the punishers are about to ask.

departments.pull_quote: The flip is the one action this deck can never take reactively. Its risk compounds every cycle it waits.
departments.note: Two spreads from the decision artifacts: 001 (turn 6 — does Forced Fruition come down against a spellslinger?) and 002 (turn 7 — when does Heliod become the Warped Eclipse?). Both carry figures re-synced to the v4 build (284067d77208 goldfish) — render them as current, verbatim. The recommendation must sit visually below the branches in both; neither dek nor headline may hint at the answers.

departments.headline: WHO BREAKS THE COURT
departments.dek: Creature wraths hit almost nothing you care about — with one seven-mana exception you must never block with — and the scariest cards against you are the ones that never use the stack at all. Can you name them before you sit down?

threats.read: Still the one. Your draw engines, all three punishers, the rocks, and the Reservoir sit in a single blast radius, while creature wraths hit a mean of 1.512 bodies by turn 6. The long game is sweep-layered four walkers deep on purpose: Jace Beleren, Jace, Wielder of Mysteries, Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim, and — new this printing — Teferi, Hero of Dominaria all survive every Supreme Verdict, including YOURS, which you can cast through their open permission. Hero of Dominaria is the mirror's best card: the +1 draws and untaps two lands at the next end step, so your clock ticks while counter mana stays open, and the -3 tucks the permanent their deck can't rebuy. The standing discipline: Hullbreaker Horror is a combo piece first and a blocker never — a wrath that takes an early 'value' Horror costs you the verified kill, not a 7-drop. Deploy in layers, and keep the kill pieces in hand until the commit turn; Enlightened Tutor makes that discipline nearly free, because the piece you haven't fetched yet is un-sweepable.
outs: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse

threats.read: Ordinary soft locks you now RACE — the kill needs the four pieces and {2}, nothing more, and Enlightened Tutor finds the missing piece through a resource-starved board. But two classes beat the line structurally, not interactively: a Rule of Law-class effect caps a 15-cast turn dead, and a per-spell tax breaks the loop's verified mana-neutrality. Against those your role flips to beatdown on the lock itself — answer the compounding second piece, not the first inconvenience: a lone Thalia is an annoyance; Thalia plus Deafening Silence is a funeral. Teferi, Hero of Dominaria's -3 is the new repeatable answer, tucking a lock piece every other turn. And you are partly the denial player yourself: Drannith Magistrate shuts off every commander and every non-hand cast, which in commander-dependent pods makes YOU the lock. Heliod's discount is the tax rebate no other deck gets.

The polarity flipped: with a verified 15-cast kill behind Abolisher's closed windows and wincon access in 49.6% of games by turn 6, you are frequently the faster, better-protected combo deck in the pod — and the racer does not durdle. Land Drannith EARLY against a known combo seat: flashback, escape, and cast-from-exile lines all die to 'from anywhere other than their hands' — though not true reanimation, which never casts. Spend the free suite (held by turn 6 in 67.2% of games) only on the card that ends the game. The standing warning survives every version: the hug layer is a liability here — Kwain stays untapped, and Forced Fruition stays in hand unless a punisher is down and you are the one about to win. And the bench holds this matchup's recorded answer: No More Lies comes in for Font of Mythos at pods where the game is decided by turn 5, because the slowest symmetric engine is pure fuel for the storm seat. Font stays maindeck by default — the swap is pod-conditional, the pilot's call, on the record.

You are the control deck and happy about it: Propaganda and The Second Doctor's rider are virtual card advantage tripled at a four-player table, Eiganjo channels away the worst attacker, and Supreme Verdict resets whatever gets through. Be honest about the v4 trade, though: Ghostly Prison went to the bench for Archmage's Charm — never-dead interaction over a third attack tax — so the pillow is one layer thinner, and its return case is exactly this pod: two or more combat seats turning sideways every turn. The ledger this matchup owns is unchanged: the kill pays 50 life three times, and the 15-cast minimum is computed FROM 32 LIFE — at 20 life it is 16 casts, at 8 it is 17, each extra cast another window. Every point of chip damage you absorb is combo disruption whether the aggro player knows it or not. Pillow hard, let Kwain and your own setup casts pad the ledger, and go a turn earlier rather than a window longer.

pilot_tips.text: Never flash the Horror in early as value into a control seat — it is the one creature you own whose death costs a verified kill instead of a card.
Against storm and spellslinger pods, hold Forced Fruition all game if you must — seven free cards per spell is a donation those decks convert faster than your punishers can tax it.

departments.pull_quote: Your life total is a combo resource. Every point of chip damage you absorb is disruption, whether they know it or not.

departments.headline: ENGINES, PUNISHERS, AND THE LAW
departments.dek: Eighty-four cards doing seven jobs: feed the table, tax the hand, buy the waiting turns, keep your draws asymmetric, say no, survive the wrath — or execute. The load-bearing cards lead, three of them wearing this printing's NEW chip — and the role histogram famously can't see half the plan.

roster.role: The court: engines that feed the table
The hug fort: gifts with riders
Interaction, resets, and the blink engine

captions.Alhammarret's Archive: **THE RIGGING:** your draws double, your lifegain doubles, and nobody else's do — Kwain pays you twice on both halves, and a first Approach banks 14. Five mana that turns every symmetric engine you run into a rigged one.
captions.The Second Doctor: **HEADS AND TAILS:** no maximum hand size means the cleanup trim never saves anyone from the Maiden — and each opponent who takes the end-step card can't attack you next turn. Heads they can't attack, tails they fall behind.
captions.Enlightened Tutor: **THE SCHEDULER:** one white mana, instant speed, any artifact or enchantment to the top — every kill piece but Hullbreaker, both named punishers, the taxes, the doublers. The tenth Game Changer, and this printing's headline swap.
captions.Drannith Magistrate: **THE LAW:** opponents can't cast from anywhere but their hands — no commanders, no flashback, no cascade. One of ten Game Changers, and in commander-dependent pods, suddenly you are the lock.
captions.Consecrated Sphinx: **THE MAGNET:** two cards to you per card an opponent draws — fourteen per opponent spell under Forced Fruition, and the strongest removal magnet you play.

pilot_tips.text: With Displacer Kitten out, any noncreature cast blinks Remora back as a new object with zero age counters — the cumulative upkeep restarts from nothing. The long-run value line is still a flagged candidate, but the object math is plain oracle text.

departments.note: Rank matters: the verified kill package leads — it is why this volume exists — then the court and the sentence; mana closes. departments.headline: A HUNDRED AND EIGHT HANDS
departments.dek: Who leads a credits page with no leader? A hundred and eight artists across 146 entries once the sideboard pool is counted — and the raw top line is half sideboard and one river painted twice. So this issue the feature follows the story: the hand that painted the kill's spine.

featured.note: Two cards, two copies, no inflation — and the two cards are the deck's entire flash-haymaker department: Hullbreaker Horror, the spine of the checker-verified table-kill, and Torrential Gearhulk, the counterspell with a 5/6 attached. In a collection this flat the feature has to be an editorial choice, so we make it honestly: the ranking's top line is Adam Paquette at five entries, but two of those are the same river painted twice — two printings of Prairie Stream — and two more live in the sideboard pool, not the 99, which is exactly why this department reads the table instead of quoting it. Count per copy and you'd crown a basic-land artist: Ron Spears' Island appears eleven times and Zoltan Boros' Plains six — repetition is printing, not authorship, so we count cards, always, and list copies as their own labeled fact. There is no Secret Lair run hiding in these numbers, no collector-number streak, no product bought whole: a hundred-plus artists across three decades of sets, from Mark Tedin's Braingeyser to this year's printings, is what a deck assembled one card at a time looks like. Velinov's Hullbreaker — a leviathan mid-lunge, painted for a horror set and reprinted into this deck's defining case file — takes the hero slot, with the artist credit and printing (INR 68) beneath it, per the convention on every hero image in this magazine.

also_worth_noting.note: Three credits, all of them in the 99: Drannith Magistrate beside Metallurgic Summonings and Teferi's Ageless Insight. Still the largest all-maindeck cluster on the page.

Painted the kill's shield: Grand Abolisher, the two-mana doorman that closes the verified line's windows. His other two credits, Ephara, God of the Polis and Jin-Gitaxias, Core Augur, sit in the sideboard pool.
Two credits split by this printing's swaps in the happy direction: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria — the promote swap's centrepiece — joins the 99, while Lay Claim stays in the pool.
Two cards, one lineage: Braingeyser and Temple Bell — the game's oldest everyone-draws job and its bell-shaped descendant, decades apart, same hand.

Two credits split the other way: Mikokoro, Center of the Sea stays maindeck — the issue's thesis painted onto a land, everyone gets a card, and it survives every board wipe in the format — while Fellwar Stone was benched this printing, carrying a verified demerit no painting could save it from.

captions.Hullbreaker Horror: **THE SPINE, SIGNED:** Svetlin Velinov's leviathan is the card six case files orbit — refuted at two pieces, verified at three, lethal at four.
captions.Torrential Gearhulk: **THE OTHER HAYMAKER:** Velinov's second credit interacts the turn it arrives — a flash 5/6 that replays a counterspell or Dig Through Time for free.

The featured pick is editorial and derives deterministically from the issue's angle (the artist of the verified kill's spine), not from a count the data doesn't support; the prose says so in as many words. Art File fast-facts from the computed credits, labeled honestly: 146 entries / 167 copies / 108 artists across the 99 plus the 61-entry refactoring pool (the 99 itself is 85 entries, 100 copies); 1 foil, 1 borderless, 15 legendary frames; top set Secrets of Strixhaven Commander at 9 entries by 9 different artists. Per-entry verification note: the eight cards swapped in across the two rebuild passes carry eight different verified signatures (Deschamps, Yanner, Briclot, Steinbauer, Villeneuve, Rallis, Ortiz, Lyon) — usable as a body-prose line, but never as a joined artist credit, since credits fields name one artist each. departments.headline: FOUR OPENERS, FOUR RULINGS
departments.dek: The sim keeps 73.4% of first sevens, so the question is rarely whether to keep — it's which of these four you would ship anyway. Rule on each before you read the bench's reason.

hands.why: Three lands, a rock, an asymmetric engine, a table engine, and something that says no — the exact bar: two to four lands, one card-flow piece, an answer. Heliod needs no help from your seven; he arrives by turn 6 in 89.6% of games on his own.

Ancient Tomb into a two-mana rock is the deck's accelerant — the line behind the 27.3% of games that land Heliod by turn 3. Kwain and Jace Beleren both count among the cheap engines worth keeping a hand for: the table draws with you, likes you for it, and feeds the punisher math anyway.

hands.verdict: SHIP — a courtroom with no plaintiffs
hands.why: Three punishers and not one card that makes anybody draw. Iron Maiden against a normal five-card hand is one damage a turn — the punishers are inert until the engine exists, and the full two-piece assembles by turn 6 in only 41.3% of games even from good hands. A hand of punishers and no engine is a mulligan in costume. Ship it.

Three lands and four cards that are all the back half of a game. Nothing here draws, taxes, or says no — and you never mulligan toward wincons anyway: access sits at 49.6% by turn 6 with Jace, Wielder of Mysteries standing in the count, and the kill pieces are what Enlightened Tutor, Long-Term Plans, and the 76.2% draw engine schedule for you in the midgame, never what your opener owes you.

captions.Mystic Remora: **THE UPGRADE:** the card that turns a marginal keep into a live one — a turn-one Remora often banks three-plus cards before the upkeep bites.

pilot_tips.text: Pay Remora's cumulative upkeep two or three times, then let it go — the ages are a fee, not a mortgage, and the cards are already banked.

departments.pull_quote: You are mulliganing toward flow plus interaction — never toward the kill.

departments.headline: OVERRULED ON APPEAL
departments.dek: Last printing this page said zero swaps left, with pride. The pilot appealed, the review charter got de-biased, and the re-run found four — two applied, two benched with their pull-in conditions on the record, plus a tutor the pool never held. The verdict changed because the process improved. That's the whole point of the process.

pilot_tips.text: Remember why Fellwar sits out: not the index's Sol Ring comparison but the verified demerit — stack 004 shows its loop cycle is 3-in, 2-out against empty opposing boards, and Thought Vessel substitutes exactly. Sleeve it back only if a third loop-capable rock slot ever opens.
The index says Mystical Tutor obsoletes it, but the supersession is narrower than it looks — Plans fetches permanents: a punisher, the Reservoir, the missing loop rock. Keep both.

Do not sleeve the Sphinx as an Abolisher backup — its static stops counterspells only, a Reservoir activation is not a cast, and 006's open windows are lost to removal and instant-speed plays no uncounterability prevents. Its real job is the recorded pod-conditional swap: in for Propaganda at two or more heavy-permission seats, where it makes the second Approach counter-proof.

Keep Font maindeck by default, but know its recorded exit: at fast-combo pods, No More Lies takes its slot — the slowest symmetric engine is pure fuel for the storm seat, and a tax counter that exiles protects your setup turns instead.

departments.pull_quote: The bench said zero swaps left. The pilot asked who audits the bench — and the de-biased re-run found four.
departments.note: Three movements, each honestly labeled. ONE — the appeal, told with pride, not apology: the previous printing's 'zero swaps' verdict was overturned by a re-verification of the 60-card bench under the de-biased charter, after the pilot challenged it; the re-run found four candidates. The two promotes are applied: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria for Secure the Wastes — a sweep-surviving clock that draws while untapping two counter-lands beats an X-spell that needs seven-plus mana and three combat steps — and Archmage's Charm for Ghostly Prison — never-dead modal interaction over a third attack tax at a draw-go table. The two pod-conditional swaps stay benched with pull-in conditions on the record: Sphinx of the Final Word for Propaganda at two-plus heavy-permission seats; No More Lies for Font of Mythos at fast-combo pods, Font maindeck by default per the pilot. And outside the pool entirely, the pilot added Enlightened Tutor for Fellwar Stone — the cut confirmed loop-safe by stack 004, Thought Vessel the exact substitute, and the Tutor the TENTH Game Changer on a floor-4 the deck already occupies. All three outgoing cards carry explicit return cases in the analysis; quote them. TWO — the index audit: the actionable debt stays paid (Worn Powerstone and Brass Infiniscope left in the previous pass); what remains is nuance — Azorius Signet's Mind Stone entry is a fair swap only if you value the cash-in over colored fixing, Counterspell's 'successors' are conditional counters by their own text, and Fellwar's index entry named Sol Ring while the real reason it sits out is the verified one. Say plainly these are similarity artifacts. Run the punisher line as the standing fast-fact: Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke, Viseling, Howling Mine, Font of Mythos — zero obsolescence entries; the old cards are the tech, not the debt. THREE — the long-term defaults, best-of as fast-facts lines: Omniscience (parked until the Approach-under-Omniscience scenario resolves), Laboratory Maniac and Blue Sun's Zenith (both ride the unverified Jace, Wielder line — one scenario decides their entire bench value), Monastery Mentor (the corrected entry: he IS a payoff on the verified loop — every artifact cast makes a prowess Monk — but hasteless tokens wait a full turn cycle the same-turn Reservoir kill never risks; verdict unchanged, scenario flagged), Deluge Virtuoso (zero triggers off an all-artifact loop). The gap-study shortlist is half-bought: Enlightened Tutor is now maindeck; Fabricate and Trouble in Pairs remain outside the collection — deck-analyst shortlist evidence, recommendations, never supersessions. Close on the one real structural exposure, loudly and unchanged: no Grand Abolisher redundancy exists anywhere in the pool — no other card restricts what opponents may do during your turn — so if the shield is answered, the fallback is the free-counter suite guarding up to fifteen open windows by hand. Acquiring a redundant effect is a decision for the pilot, outside this analysis's constraint.

departments.headline: SIX FILES, ONE EXECUTION
departments.dek: 151 verbatim citations across six case files — and, by pure coincidence the bench refuses to stop enjoying, 151 is also the number the kill's ledger must clear from one life. A-001 overturns the database. A-005 overturns our own best idea. A-006 executes.
departments.note: Renderer-generated from the checker-passed artifacts; nothing summarized, truncated, or paraphrased. Case order A-001 through A-006, presented as the completed arc across linked file tabs: refute the two-card claim (A-001), establish the three-card engine (A-004), refute the engine's dreamed upgrade (A-005), then promote the engine to a complete table-kill with an exact ledger (A-006) — with A-002 and A-003 as the standing plans B and C. Case status lines where the artifacts record them: A-003, A-004, and A-006 each passed on the second iteration, A-005 on the first; say so — the checker sending work back is the reason the stamp means anything (A-001 and A-002 record no iteration count; print none). Rules version June 19, 2026 on every file. The v4 swaps touched no case file — every card the six artifacts turn on is still in the 99, and A-004's conditional-rock finding about Fellwar Stone became this printing's cut: the file predicted the benching before the pilot made it. Print that in the margin; it is the evidence system working forward. Two more honesty lines: the bracket report still lists the refuted Hullbreaker + Sol Ring pair among its floor-4 drivers — the floor is 4 regardless, on ten Game Changers and on kill content that stack 006 has verified for real, and those are the drivers this magazine cites. And A-006's file carries its own caveat in the checker's voice: the ledger is exact, the windows are open, and the Abolisher shield named in its summary has not itself been walked against every out.

Next issue is TO BE ANNOUNCED per issue.json — run the teaser as authored, do not invent a deck. Colophon carries the rules version (June 19, 2026), the decklist sha256 (284067d77208…), seed 42, and the Fan Content Policy line — plus the provenance this four-times-stamped volume owes its readers, straight from HISTORY.md's four entries: initial import, the pilot's corrected build definition, the five approved tier-4 swaps, and now the re-verification's two promotes plus the pilot's Enlightened Tutor after the 'zero swaps left' verdict was overturned on appeal. Close the loop on the angle in one line above the colophon: court adjourned — conviction upheld on appeal, and the appeal made it stronger.

rhythm_notes: The canonical order alternates cleanly: By the Numbers (dense analysis, five callouts carrying the flat-trade ledger) hands off to The Kill, whose eight callout-steps read as narrative — the built-in breather doing its job. The Kill is the peak and keeps the most ambitious layout of the volume: A-006's execution-ledger spread as the marquee, the engine and the two plan-B lines behind it, and the refutation pair as the linked double spread that keeps the credibility page. Politics (reflection, now six callouts with the tutor-tell added) recovers from the peak, What's Your Play re-engages, Know Your Enemy's four threat-boxes (reference) are followed by two deliberately low-intensity browsing pages — The 99 and the breadth-story Featured Artist, whose pull quote is the issue's quietest page, placed there on purpose. Keep or Ship re-activates the reader before Upgrade Watch, which is light in layout but now carries the issue's best process story — the verdict we overturned ourselves — and Judge's Desk stays opt-in manila at the back. The overturning is told at three depths without repetition: one cover tease, Upgrade Watch's full three-movement account, and the Back Page's one-line provenance close.
gaps: The Abolisher-airtightness scenario remains the highest-value stack to resolve: stack 006 names Abolisher as the window-closer but no walkthrough scopes the shield against the channel-land loophole (Otawara activates from a card in hand, not from an artifact/creature/enchantment permanent) — it gates how confidently Politics and The Kill may say 'uninterruptable', and the sideboard analysis flags it explicitly.

Remaining candidate lines are teased only as candidates: Alhammarret's Archive halving the 006 ledger, the Drannith stranding lock with Verdict/Path (CR 903.9 walkthrough), the Jace, Wielder of Mysteries self-deck win (one scenario now decides both Laboratory Maniac's and Blue Sun's Zenith's entire bench value), the Monastery Mentor loop-payoff line (new this pass — corrected from 'no second payoff exists in the pool'), Approach under Omniscience, the Kitten/Remora age-counter reset, Psychosis Crawler + mass X-draw, Smothering Tithe arithmetic, and the Fraying Sanity cleanup question.

No Grand Abolisher redundancy exists anywhere in the pool — the verified kill's one shield has no backup, and Sphinx of the Final Word is explicitly not it (a Reservoir activation is not a cast). Acquiring one is outside the sideboard constraint; flagged to the pilot as the deck's one real structural exposure, and Upgrade Watch says it loudly.

Strategy DB holes the frame names: no school for priority-window management on sorcery-speed loops (stack 006 made this the deck's central play skill), none for group-hug donation risk, none for empty-library win lines, none for topdeck tutors (to-top vs to-hand — Enlightened Tutor's evaluation leans on redundancy-vs-tutors, which assumes to-hand copies), and racing-under-tax math remains queued in PLAN.md. Coaching departments ground in adjacent schools (storm-math, pivot-window, answer-economy, redundancy-vs-tutors) and say so.

The goldfish model does not play tutors: Enlightened Tutor counts in the wincon-access group only as a drawn card, so the flat 49.6%-vs-50.1% access reading understates the swap's real effect by construction. By the Numbers states this in the assumptions box; a tutor-aware target model is a simulator feature request, not an editorial fix.
